claims.wording: LatentGuard-VLA implemented generic exact-state paired replay and physically validated it for a pinned ManiSkill PickCube integration.
claims.scope: ManiSkill PickCube adapter version 1.1.1 under its content-bound compatibility identity and 1e-6 complete-state runtime comparison contract.
limitations: The physical result does not automatically extend to other simulators, tasks, controllers, or adapters.

claims.wording: The project generated thousands of strong simulator-verified PickCube counterfactual outcomes with trajectory-grouped provenance.
claims.scope: The accepted M3A state-indexed dataset contains 2,880 evaluated corrupted proposals from 60 source trajectories and 360 anchors.
limitations: Scale comes from synthetic action corruptions in one fixed PickCube task, not independent robot tasks.

claims.wording: Structured state-plus-action failure prediction was learnable in the fixed PickCube corruption scope.
claims.scope: Five fixed seeds, validation-only architecture selection, and untouched test evaluation on the accepted M3A dataset.
limitations: The learned result does not establish visual, language, cross-task, real-robot, or general-safety performance.

claims.wording: Blind verifier-guided one-shot candidate selection outperformed deterministic random selection on untouched PickCube groups.
claims.scope: M3C identical eight-candidate pools across 360 groups; selection was frozen before outcomes were loaded.
limitations: One-shot success does not imply performance under repeated intervention; the joint MLP, not the temporal model, was the strongest learned selector.

claims.wording: Frozen visual one-shot selection remained strong under predeclared camera and lighting shifts and outperformed random selection.
claims.scope: M4B external evaluation on the fixed M4A camera rig and render domains; no external data was used for training or tuning.
limitations: The result is one-shot and narrowly rendered; it was not statistically better than action-only selection.

claims.wording: Content-bound transactional publication and zero-work resume were validated across the largest data and benchmark runs.
claims.scope: Accepted M3A and M4D compact evidence, with analogous accepted resume reports in intervening milestones.
limitations: This establishes application-level idempotence for the tested workflows, not a universal distributed-systems durability guarantee.

claims.wording: The conservative M4D gate preserved clean nominal PickCube performance without false intervention.
claims.scope: Primary gated direct visual selector on clean canonical M4D episodes.
limitations: Clean preservation alone does not establish fault detection or general safety.

claims.wording: Conservative gating produced a measurable but limited benefit over accepting injected nominal faults.
claims.scope: M4D controlled injected-fault canonical schedule with a frozen gate and paired source-trajectory bootstrap.
limitations: Success remained below ungated direct and always-fallback baselines, and override recall was only 4.03 percent.

claims.wording: Visual information adds deployment value beyond actions alone.
claims.scope: M4B external one-shot comparison only.
limitations: The visual-minus-action-only confidence interval included zero; repeated visual intervention also underperformed action-only in M4C.

claims.wording: Privileged structured-teacher distillation improves deployment behavior.
claims.scope: M4B internal prediction and one-shot evidence, tested further in M4C closed loop.
limitations: The distilled visual selector did not beat the privileged or fixed baselines under repeated intervention.

claims.wording: Verifier-guided shielding improves full closed-loop control.
claims.scope: M4C repeated intervention and M4D controlled injected-fault evaluation.
limitations: M4C overall targets failed, while M4D improved only over accept-nominal and missed four predeclared targets.

claims.wording: Conservative gating approaches trusted fallback performance while intervening less.
claims.scope: M4D injected-fault canonical evaluation.
limitations: The 0.20 success-rate gap to always fallback was material; the within-0.05 target failed.

claims.wording: The distilled visual shield outperforms the fixed primary in repeated closed-loop control.
claims.scope: M4C canonical repeated-intervention benchmark.
limitations: Observed success was 0.266667 lower than fixed primary and intervention was 93.48 percent.

claims.wording: LatentGuard-VLA establishes general robot safety.
claims.scope: Outside the frozen PickCube evidence boundary.
limitations: No general hazard model, safety certification, or broad task distribution was evaluated.

claims.wording: The system is robust on real robots.
claims.scope: No real-robot execution occurred.
limitations: All physical evaluation used the pinned ManiSkill PickCube simulator integration.

claims.wording: The verifier transfers across robot tasks.
claims.scope: Only PickCube was evaluated.
limitations: No second task adapter or untouched task distribution was run.

claims.wording: The verifier transfers across robot embodiments.
claims.scope: Only one robot/controller contract was evaluated.
limitations: No cross-robot dataset, calibration, or control integration exists.

claims.wording: The results demonstrate VLA generalization.
claims.scope: No learned VLA policy was executed.
limitations: The project evaluated solver-derived action candidates rather than arbitrary VLA outputs.

claims.wording: The shield supports arbitrary motion replanning.
claims.scope: Fixed eight-candidate chunk pools and a fixed-primary fallback only.
limitations: The selector cannot synthesize arbitrary new trajectories.

claims.wording: The verifier detects real hardware faults.
claims.scope: M4D used controlled action-level fault injection in simulation.
limitations: Injected nominal-action perturbations are not measurements of actuator, sensor, network, or hardware failures.

claims.wording: The verifier performs language-conditioned verification.
claims.scope: No language input was authorized as a deployable feature.
limitations: No language model, instruction distribution, or language-grounded evidence was evaluated.

claims.wording: LatentGuard-VLA improves LangMani policy performance.
claims.scope: LangMani remained outside the frozen PickCube line.
limitations: No LangMani adapter, policy, data, or benchmark was executed.
